title: Stop counting worktree-cap refusals as runner deaths; add re-dispatch backoff
goal:
Stop counting worktree-cap refusals as runner deaths; add re-dispatch backoff (S1).

Source research: task 2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4 ("noticing a high level of interruptions"). Read docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md and the cited GUIDE before coding. Survey answers (if any) live in docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE_SURVEY.md. Section: RESPONSE.md S1, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/GUIDE-01-worktree-cap-loop.md, WIDE_NET Cause 1 + amplifier. Survey: q1 (cap refusals must never park), q2 (backoff for repeat resumes).

Evidence: "All 49 reasoned interrupts are WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED refusals, yet interruptExecution increments runnerInterruptCount unconditionally, so five capacity refusals park the task as a runner-death-loop (42 escalations fleet-wide). And every interrupt re-dispatches in ~150ms with Rule-0 priority, so the same still-full runner re-claims instantly." Exhibits: tasks 350ca162 (12x), db24c124 (9x), 7b69d365 (6x).

Change (backend, api/): (1) api/flow/executionLedger.js interruptExecution: do not increment runnerInterruptCount / escalate when reason starts with "Runner workdir unavailable:"; record on a separate capacityRefusalCount with its own operator threshold. (2) scheduler (api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js / findResumedCandidate.js): after N consecutive resumes of same task+stage, delay re-dispatch (30s -> 5min) and/or sort behind fresh work, prefer a DIFFERENT runner than the refuser; keep first resume fast. (3) keep runner-death-loop parking for true death streaks (api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js).

Tests (red first): api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js (5 cap interrupts -> count 0, no park); api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js (fresh work wins after N resumes); keep pin: 5 bare/crash interrupts still park (executionLedger.test.js ~L778). Confirm bug locally via GUIDE-01 section 3 snippet first.

Coordination: open ticket e3d4e9db adds RUNNER-side setup-failure backoff - complementary, do not duplicate it; this ticket is the BACKEND counter exclusion + scheduler backoff. Backend-only, no runner rollout needed. Confirm with GUIDE-07 section 5 fleet script: escalated drops, with_reason stays visible.

KAINBAIN_REASON: <what is wrong, concretely — file, test, behaviour>
KAINBAIN_FIX: <how the next attempt should fix it — what to change, run, or check>

**Important:** The verdict block must be plain text. Do NOT surround it with triple backticks, quote blocks, or any other formatting. The engine only recognizes lines that start with `KAINBAIN_VERDICT:`, `KAINBAIN_REASON:`, or `KAINBAIN_FIX:` (case-insensitive) followed by a colon.

Rules:

- **Agent stages only.** A verdict is optional guidance for AGENT stages.

reports.content:
# Implementation plan — S1: stop counting worktree-cap refusals as runner deaths; re-dispatch backoff

Task: `3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7`. Backend-only (`api/`), no runner rollout needed.

## 1. Goal and scope

- (1) `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution`: do not increment
  `runnerInterruptCount` / escalate when the reason starts with
  `"Runner workdir unavailable:"`; count those on a separate
  `capacityRefusalCount` with its own operator-visible threshold (never parks).
- (2) Scheduler (`api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js` /
  `findResumedCandidate.js`): after N consecutive resumes of the same
  task+stage, delay re-dispatch (30s doubling to 5min cap) and/or sort behind
  fresh work; prefer a DIFFERENT runner than the refuser; keep the first
  resume fast.
- (3) Keep runner-death-loop parking for true death streaks
  (`api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js`).

Non-goals / coordination: ticket `e3d4e9db` adds RUNNER-side setup-failure
backoff — complementary, do not duplicate it. This ticket is the BACKEND
counter exclusion + scheduler backoff only.

## 2. Input status (read before starting)

### 2.1 Grill survey (SURVEY.md) — UNANSWERED

`docs/tasks/3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7/SURVEY.md` round 1 has five
questions and `"answers": {}` — no answers were recorded. The plan below
adopts each question's Recommended option as the working default, and every
affected phase lists the survey question it depends on so an implementer can
re-check if answers arrive later:

| Survey q | Default (Recommended) | Drives phase |
|---|---|---|
| q1 cap refusals never park | Yes, never park; separate visibility-only counter | Phase 3 |
| q2 backoff shape | First retry instant; after 3 consecutive resumes 30s doubling to 5min; fresh work first | Phase 4 |
| q3 backoff scope | ALL repeatedly resumed tasks (covers reason-less interrupts from old runners) | Phase 4 |
| q4 runner avoidance | Hide task from refusing runner ~2min (backend cannot direct-assign) | Phase 4, step 4.4 |
| q5 guardrails | Bare/crash streaks still park after 5; capacity counter never parks | Phase 5 (pin tests) |

If survey answers arrive before implementation, re-read this table first: a
non-Recommended answer changes only its row's phase, not the whole plan.

### 2.2 Source research — MISSING from this checkout

The ticket cites `docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/`
(`RESPONSE.md`, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`,
`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`, `GUIDE-01-worktree-cap-loop.md`, `GUIDE-07` §5 fleet
script). None of these exist in this checkout (`ls docs/tasks/2e663986*`
fails; no `GUIDE-*` anywhere under `docs/`; ticket `e3d4e9db` also absent).
So Phase 0 reconstructs the two load-bearing artifacts locally instead of
blocking: a GUIDE-01-§3-style repro snippet and a GUIDE-07-§5-style fleet
check. If the research task is later fetched, diff its S1 section against
§5–§7 and update this plan.

## 3. Verified current-state findings (code read, not assumed)

- Counting: `interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:644-651`)
  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally and escalates at
  `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`. Confirmed — matches the ticket's evidence.
- Parking: `isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57` parks at
  `runnerInterruptCount >= 5` with reason `runner-death-loop`.
- Reason wire: runner sends `` `Runner workdir unavailable: ${err.message}` ``
  on `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` (`runner/daemon.js:2306`) via
  `client.interrupt({ reason })`; ledger stores it trimmed to 500 chars in
  history (`executionLedger.js:653-658`). Prefix match on
  `"Runner workdir unavailable:"` is therefore stable.
- Rule-0 priority: `findResumedCandidate.js:82-94` sorts ALL resumable
  interruptions oldest-first and `findNextCandidateTask.js:54-55` returns the
  Rule-0 hit ahead of everything, with no resume-count or delay concept.
- Runner re-claim path: runners claim from `scanClaimableTasks`
  (`api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js`), which only lists `in_stage`
  tasks sorted via the shared `sortCentralQueue` seam — the ~150ms
  re-dispatch loop runs through `scheduleTick` → `autoResumeTask` (flip to
  `in_stage`) → immediate re-offer, which is why the same still-full runner
  re-claims. Any delay/sort fix must cover BOTH `findResumedCandidate`
  (embedded) and `scanClaimableTasks` (fleet), or the loop survives on the
  uncovered path.
- Existing pin tests: `executionLedger.test.js:765-797` (escalation at 5, the
  "~L778" pin) and `taskScheduler.test.js:569-584` (death-loop parking at 5).
  Both must keep passing unchanged.
- No existing resume-count/backoff state: no `consecutiveResumes`-like field
  exists on tasks; this plan introduces one (see Phase 4).

## 4. Work order rationale (big / research pieces first)

"Make change easy, then make the change": Phase 0 (research + repro) and
Phase 1 (test-only refactors: pure helpers + harnesses) come before any
behavior change, are individually committable, and de-risk the later phases.
Ledger exclusion (Phase 3) lands before scheduler backoff (Phase 4) because
it is smaller, independently verifiable, and removes the parking harm even if
backoff slips.

## 5. Phase 0 — Research recovery + bug confirmation (do first)

Goal: replace the missing GUIDE artifacts with local equivalents and confirm
the bug red before touching behavior.

- 0.1 Reconstruct the GUIDE-01 §3 snippet as a throwaway node script (under
  `/tmp`, not committed): build a minimal `claimStore`/`taskStore` harness
  (copy the `claimed(ctx)` pattern at the top of `executionLedger.test.js`),
  call `interruptExecution` 5x with
  `reason: "Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5)"` on the
  same task+stage, and assert the CURRENT (buggy) outcome:
  `runnerInterruptCount === 5`, `escalated === true`, and
  `isAutoResumableWithReason(task, {type:"agent"}).reason ===
  "runner-death-loop"`. Keep this script for Phase 6 re-run (expect flipped
  assertions).
- 0.2 Reconstruct the GUIDE-07 §5 fleet check as a script: scan task docs (or
  the live API if available) counting `escalated` / `with_reason` interrupts;
  record the before numbers (ticket claims 42 escalations fleet-wide, all 49
  reasoned interrupts cap refusals). After the fix, escalated must drop while
  `with_reason` stays visible.
- 0.3 Measure the re-dispatch interval: time interrupt → `scheduleTick`
  re-offer on a scratch task to confirm the "~150ms Rule-0 re-claim" claim;
  record the number in the implementation notes.
- 0.4 Decision checkpoint: confirm survey defaults from §2.1 still hold (or
  apply any newly arrived answers to the table).

Exit criteria: §0.1 script demonstrates parking after 5 cap refusals on the
unmodified tree.

## 6. Phase 1 — Make the change easy (no behavior change)

Small, test-covered refactors that the later phases plug into. Each step must
leave the full suite green on its own.

- 1.1 Extract a pure reason classifier `isCapacityRefusalReason(reason)`
  (new file `api/flow/capacityRefusal.js`, one function per file per repo
  convention + `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs`): returns true iff
  the trimmed reason starts with `"Runner workdir unavailable:"`. Cover with
  a unit test (prefix, case where reason is null/empty/other, leading
  whitespace). No callers yet.
- 1.2 Extract the interrupt-count/escalate block in `interruptExecution`
  (`executionLedger.js:644-665`) into a shape the ledger method still calls
  identically (pure helper or clearly delimited section), so Phase 3's branch
  is a 10-line diff, not a rewrite. Full `api` suite green before/after.
- 1.3 Add a shared scheduler-test harness if none fits: `findResumedCandidate`
  and `scanClaimableTasks` tests need a fake store with
  `projectStore.listProjects`, `listTasks`, `isTaskBlocked`, `claimStore`.
  Reuse the seed pattern in `api/flow/taskScheduler.test.js` (~L640-700);
  only add a helper if two new test files would otherwise duplicate it.
- 1.4 Constants: decide names now so tests can import them —
  `MAX_CAPACITY_REFUSALS_BEFORE_NOTE` (operator visibility note, e.g. 5;
  never parks) and backoff constants (`RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD = 3`,
  `RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 30_000`, `RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 300_000`).
  Put ledger constants with the ledger, scheduler constants in the new
  backoff module.

## 7. Phase 2 — Red tests first (must fail before Phase 3/4)

Write these before the behavior change and watch them fail:

- 2.1 `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js`:
  - 5 consecutive cap-refusal interrupts on same task+stage →
    `runnerInterruptCount` stays 0 (or absent), `escalated === false`,
    `interruptEscalations` counter stays 0, status still `interrupted`,
    reason still recorded in history, `capacityRefusalCount === 5`.
  - Mixed streak: cap refusals do not reset a genuine death streak (decide
    and document: recommended — a cap refusal neither increments nor resets
    `runnerInterruptCount`; a completion/stage-change still resets both).
  - Cap-refusal streak across a stage change restarts `capacityRefusalCount`
    per task+stage, mirroring `runnerInterruptCount` semantics.
- 2.2 `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js`:
  - Fresh `in_stage` work wins over a task with ≥ N consecutive resumes
    (survey q2/q3 default: threshold 3, all resume kinds).
  - First and second resumes keep Rule-0 priority (fast path pinned).
  - Backoff delay: a 3rd-resume task is skipped until 30s elapsed, 4th until
    60s, capped at 5min (inject `now` — never wall-clock in the sort).
  - Different-runner preference / refusing-runner hide (survey q4): task
    hidden from the refusing runner for ~2min while visible to others.
- 2.3 Keep-pins (must stay green throughout, no edits): the 5x bare-interrupt
  escalation test (`executionLedger.test.js:765-797`), the 5x death-loop
  parking test (`taskScheduler.test.js:569-584`), and the reasoned-history
  test (`executionLedger.test.js:746-763`, updated only if its
  `interruptCount: 1` expectation legitimately becomes 0 — prefer updating
  that one assertion with a comment over weakening the test).

## 8. Phase 3 — Ledger: exclude cap refusals from death counting

File: `api/flow/executionLedger.js` (`interruptExecution`, ~L639-678).

- 3.1 Branch on `isCapacityRefusalReason(reason)`:
  - Cap refusal: leave `runnerInterruptCount`/`runnerInterruptStage`
    untouched; maintain `task.capacityRefusalCount` /
    `task.capacityRefusalStage` with the same per-task+stage consecutive
    semantics (stage change restarts at 1); still set
    `status = "interrupted"`, still record history with the reason, still
    `interrupts += 1`; add a `capacityRefusals += 1` monitor counter.
  - Return shape: keep `{ interrupted, interruptCount, escalated }` and add
    `capacityRefusal: true, capacityRefusalCount` so callers/tests can tell.
- 3.2 Operator visibility (survey q1/q5): at `capacityRefusalCount ===
  MAX_CAPACITY_REFUSALS_BEFORE_NOTE`, push a history note ("capacity
  refusals noted … never parks") — visibility only, no escalation counter,
  no parking hook.
- 3.3 Reset semantics: `completeExecution` clears the capacity fields exactly
  like it clears `runnerInterruptCount`/`runnerInterruptStage`
  (`executionLedger.js:540-543`). Document the mixed-streak rule from 2.1.
- 3.4 Re-run Phase 0 script: 5 cap interrupts → count 0, no park. Run
  `npm run test --prefix api -- executionLedger` + full `npm run test:api`.

## 9. Phase 4 — Scheduler: re-dispatch backoff + fresh-work priority

Survey defaults: q2 (3 strikes, 30s doubling to 5min, fresh first), q3 (all
resumes), q4 (hide from refuser ~2min). New state must be durable on the task
(it already persists via `_saveTaskMarkdown`) and time-injectable.

- 4.1 Track consecutive resumes per task+stage: add
  `task.consecutiveResumes` / `task.consecutiveResumeStage`, incremented in
  `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) when the stage
  matches (else reset to 1), cleared on completion/stage advancement. New
  pure module `api/flow/scheduler/resumeBackoff.js`: `resumeBackoffMs(task,
  stageId, nowMs)` → 0 below threshold, else
  `min(30s * 2^(n-3), 5min)`. Unit-test the curve incl. cap and garbage
  timestamps (follow the `interruptionTimestampMs` collapse-to-0 pattern).
- 4.2 Enforce the delay in `findResumedCandidate.js`: skip candidates whose
  `now - interruptedAt < resumeBackoffMs(...)`. Thread an injectable `now`
  (param defaulting to `Date.now()`) from `findNextCandidateTask` and
  `scheduleTick` so tests pin exact boundaries. First resume (count < 3)
  keeps today's instant Rule-0 path — no behavior change there.
- 4.3 Fresh work wins: when a resumed candidate is in backoff, `Rule 0` must
  not shadow fresh work — the skip in 4.2 already lets Rules 1–3 run; add the
  explicit test from 2.2 proving a fresh `in_stage` task dispatches while a
  backed-off resume waits. ALSO apply the same skip in
  `scanClaimableTasks.js` (fleet path): without it the runner fleet still
  re-claims instantly and the fix only covers the embedded scheduler.
- 4.4 Prefer a different runner (survey q4): on a cap refusal, record
  `task.lastCapacityRefusal = { runnerId, at }` in the ledger; both
  `findResumedCandidate` (embedded: skip when the only claimant would be that
  runner — only if the candidate-selection context knows the runner, else
  skip this sub-step for embedded) and `scanClaimableTasks` (fleet: filter
  the task from listings for that runner for ~2min; needs the requesting
  runner id in `opts`) honor the hide window. If plumbing the runner id
  through proves invasive, implement fleet-side only and note embedded as a
  follow-up — but do not silently drop q4; record the decision.
- 4.5 `isAutoResumableWithReason.js`: NO change to the death-loop branch
  except confirming it keys only off `runnerInterruptCount` (never the new
  capacity counter). Add a comment citing this task.

## 10. Phase 5 — Assurance: tests, gates, and fleet confirmation

- 5.1 Red→green: the Phase 2 tests fail on the base tree (record the failure
  output in the task notes) and pass after Phases 3–4. Pin tests from 2.3
  pass unmodified (except the single documented assertion if needed).
- 5.2 Full gates, in order: `npm run test:api`, `npm run test:frontend`
  (untouched but cheap), `npm run lint:api`,
  `node scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs`, plus the repo's doc checks
  if JSDoc/examples were touched (`npm run docs:check`).
- 5.3 Fleet confirmation (GUIDE-07 §5 equivalent): re-run the Phase 0.2
  script — escalated count must drop toward zero for cap-driven tasks while
  `with_reason` history stays visible; re-run the 0.3 timing check — repeat
  resumes now observe the backoff curve while first resumes stay fast.
- 5.4 Edge sweep (each gets a test or a written reason it needs none):
  null/empty/other reasons, reason with leading whitespace, stage change
  mid-streak, completion clearing both counters, corrupt `updatedAt`,
  backoff cap at 5min, hide-window expiry, old runners sending no reason
  (covered by q3-all-resumes default).

## 11. Documentation plan

- 11.1 Code-adjacent: JSDoc `MARK` blocks on the new classifier, backoff
  module, and new task fields (repo convention); update the `G7` /
  `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS` comment in `executionLedger.js` to describe the
  exclusion.
- 11.2 Task notes: record Phase 0 before/after numbers, the red-test failure
  output, and any survey-answer deltas in this task's docs folder.

1|# Implementation plan — S1: stop counting worktree-cap refusals as runner deaths; re-dispatch backoff
2|
3|Task: `3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7`. Backend-only (`api/`), no runner rollout needed.
4|
5|## 1. Goal and scope
6|
7|- (1) `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution`: do not increment
8|  `runnerInterruptCount` / escalate when the reason starts with
9|  `"Runner workdir unavailable:"`; count those on a separate
10|  `capacityRefusalCount` with its own operator-visible threshold (never parks).
11|- (2) Scheduler (`api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js` /
12|  `findResumedCandidate.js`): after N consecutive resumes of the same
13|  task+stage, delay re-dispatch (30s doubling to 5min cap) and/or sort behind
14|  fresh work; prefer a DIFFERENT runner than the refuser; keep the first
15|  resume fast.
16|- (3) Keep runner-death-loop parking for true death streaks
17|  (`api/flow/scheduler/isAutoResumableWithReason.js`).
18|
19|Non-goals / coordination: ticket `e3d4e9db` adds RUNNER-side setup-failure
20|backoff — complementary, do not duplicate it. This ticket is the BACKEND
21|counter exclusion + scheduler backoff only.
22|
23|## 2. Input status (read before starting)
24|
25|### 2.1 Grill survey (SURVEY.md) — UNANSWERED
26|
27|`docs/tasks/3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7/SURVEY.md` round 1 has five
28|questions and `"answers": {}` — no answers were recorded. The plan below
29|adopts each question's Recommended option as the working default, and every
30|affected phase lists the survey question it depends on so an implementer can
31|re-check if answers arrive later:
32|
33|| Survey q | Default (Recommended) | Drives phase |
34||---|---|---|
35|| q1 cap refusals never park | Yes, never park; separate visibility-only counter | Phase 3 |
36|| q2 backoff shape | First retry instant; after 3 consecutive resumes 30s doubling to 5min; fresh work first | Phase 4 |
37|| q3 backoff scope | ALL repeatedly resumed tasks (covers reason-less interrupts from old runners) | Phase 4 |
38|| q4 runner avoidance | Hide task from refusing runner ~2min (backend cannot direct-assign) | Phase 4, step 4.4 |
39|| q5 guardrails | Bare/crash streaks still park after 5; capacity counter never parks | Phase 5 (pin tests) |
40|
41|If survey answers arrive before implementation, re-read this table first: a
42|non-Recommended answer changes only its row's phase, not the whole plan.
43|
44|### 2.2 Source research — MISSING from this checkout
45|
46|The ticket cites `docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/`
47|(`RESPONSE.md`, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`, `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md`,
48|`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md`, `GUIDE-01-worktree-cap-loop.md`, `GUIDE-07` §5 fleet
49|script). None of these exist in this checkout (`ls docs/tasks/2e663986*`
50|fails; no `GUIDE-*` anywhere under `docs/`; ticket `e3d4e9db` also absent).
51|So Phase 0 reconstructs the two load-bearing artifacts locally instead of
52|blocking: a GUIDE-01-§3-style repro snippet and a GUIDE-07-§5-style fleet
53|check. If the research task is later fetched, diff its S1 section against
54|§5–§7 and update this plan.
55|
56|## 3. Verified current-state findings (code read, not assumed)
57|
58|- Counting: `interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:644-651`)
59|  increments `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally and escalates at
60|  `MAX_RUNNER_INTERRUPTS = 5`. Confirmed — matches the ticket's evidence.
61|- Parking: `isAutoResumableWithReason.js:52-57` parks at
62|  `runnerInterruptCount >= 5` with reason `runner-death-loop`.
63|- Reason wire: runner sends `` `Runner workdir unavailable: ${err.message}` ``
64|  on `WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED` (`runner/daemon.js:2306`) via
65|  `client.interrupt({ reason })`; ledger stores it trimmed to 500 chars in
66|  history (`executionLedger.js:653-658`). Prefix match on
67|  `"Runner workdir unavailable:"` is therefore stable.
68|- Rule-0 priority: `findResumedCandidate.js:82-94` sorts ALL resumable
69|  interruptions oldest-first and `findNextCandidateTask.js:54-55` returns the
70|  Rule-0 hit ahead of everything, with no resume-count or delay concept.
71|- Runner re-claim path: runners claim from `scanClaimableTasks`
72|  (`api/flow/dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.js`), which only lists `in_stage`
73|  tasks sorted via the shared `sortCentralQueue` seam — the ~150ms
74|  re-dispatch loop runs through `scheduleTick` → `autoResumeTask` (flip to
75|  `in_stage`) → immediate re-offer, which is why the same still-full runner
76|  re-claims. Any delay/sort fix must cover BOTH `findResumedCandidate`
77|  (embedded) and `scanClaimableTasks` (fleet), or the loop survives on the
78|  uncovered path.
79|- Existing pin tests: `executionLedger.test.js:765-797` (escalation at 5, the
80|  "~L778" pin) and `taskScheduler.test.js:569-584` (death-loop parking at 5).
81|  Both must keep passing unchanged.
82|- No existing resume-count/backoff state: no `consecutiveResumes`-like field
83|  exists on tasks; this plan introduces one (see Phase 4).
84|
85|## 4. Work order rationale (big / research pieces first)
86|
87|"Make change easy, then make the change": Phase 0 (research + repro) and
88|Phase 1 (test-only refactors: pure helpers + harnesses) come before any
89|behavior change, are individually committable, and de-risk the later phases.
90|Ledger exclusion (Phase 3) lands before scheduler backoff (Phase 4) because
91|it is smaller, independently verifiable, and removes the parking harm even if
92|backoff slips.
93|
94|## 5. Phase 0 — Research recovery + bug confirmation (do first)
95|
96|Goal: replace the missing GUIDE artifacts with local equivalents and confirm
97|the bug red before touching behavior.
98|
99|- 0.1 Reconstruct the GUIDE-01 §3 snippet as a throwaway node script (under
100|  `/tmp`, not committed): build a minimal `claimStore`/`taskStore` harness
101|  (copy the `claimed(ctx)` pattern at the top of `executionLedger.test.js`),
102|  call `interruptExecution` 5x with
103|  `reason: "Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5)"` on the
104|  same task+stage, and assert the CURRENT (buggy) outcome:
105|  `runnerInterruptCount === 5`, `escalated === true`, and
106|  `isAutoResumableWithReason(task, {type:"agent"}).reason ===
107|  "runner-death-loop"`. Keep this script for Phase 6 re-run (expect flipped
108|  assertions).
109|- 0.2 Reconstruct the GUIDE-07 §5 fleet check as a script: scan task docs (or
110|  the live API if available) counting `escalated` / `with_reason` interrupts;
111|  record the before numbers (ticket claims 42 escalations fleet-wide, all 49
112|  reasoned interrupts cap refusals). After the fix, escalated must drop while
113|  `with_reason` stays visible.
114|- 0.3 Measure the re-dispatch interval: time interrupt → `scheduleTick`
115|  re-offer on a scratch task to confirm the "~150ms Rule-0 re-claim" claim;
116|  record the number in the implementation notes.
117|- 0.4 Decision checkpoint: confirm survey defaults from §2.1 still hold (or
118|  apply any newly arrived answers to the table).
119|
120|Exit criteria: §0.1 script demonstrates parking after 5 cap refusals on the
121|unmodified tree.
122|
123|## 6. Phase 1 — Make the change easy (no behavior change)
124|
125|Small, test-covered refactors that the later phases plug into. Each step must
126|leave the full suite green on its own.
127|
128|- 1.1 Extract a pure reason classifier `isCapacityRefusalReason(reason)`
129|  (new file `api/flow/capacityRefusal.js`, one function per file per repo
130|  convention + `scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs`): returns true iff
131|  the trimmed reason starts with `"Runner workdir unavailable:"`. Cover with
132|  a unit test (prefix, case where reason is null/empty/other, leading
133|  whitespace). No callers yet.
134|- 1.2 Extract the interrupt-count/escalate block in `interruptExecution`
135|  (`executionLedger.js:644-665`) into a shape the ledger method still calls
136|  identically (pure helper or clearly delimited section), so Phase 3's branch
137|  is a 10-line diff, not a rewrite. Full `api` suite green before/after.
138|- 1.3 Add a shared scheduler-test harness if none fits: `findResumedCandidate`
139|  and `scanClaimableTasks` tests need a fake store with
140|  `projectStore.listProjects`, `listTasks`, `isTaskBlocked`, `claimStore`.
141|  Reuse the seed pattern in `api/flow/taskScheduler.test.js` (~L640-700);
142|  only add a helper if two new test files would otherwise duplicate it.
143|- 1.4 Constants: decide names now so tests can import them —
144|  `MAX_CAPACITY_REFUSALS_BEFORE_NOTE` (operator visibility note, e.g. 5;
145|  never parks) and backoff constants (`RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD = 3`,
146|  `RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 30_000`, `RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 300_000`).
147|  Put ledger constants with the ledger, scheduler constants in the new
148|  backoff module.
149|
150|## 7. Phase 2 — Red tests first (must fail before Phase 3/4)
151|
152|Write these before the behavior change and watch them fail:
153|
154|- 2.1 `api/flow/executionLedger.capInterruptLoop.test.js`:
155|  - 5 consecutive cap-refusal interrupts on same task+stage →
156|    `runnerInterruptCount` stays 0 (or absent), `escalated === false`,
157|    `interruptEscalations` counter stays 0, status still `interrupted`,
158|    reason still recorded in history, `capacityRefusalCount === 5`.
159|  - Mixed streak: cap refusals do not reset a genuine death streak (decide
160|    and document: recommended — a cap refusal neither increments nor resets
161|    `runnerInterruptCount`; a completion/stage-change still resets both).
162|  - Cap-refusal streak across a stage change restarts `capacityRefusalCount`
163|    per task+stage, mirroring `runnerInterruptCount` semantics.
164|- 2.2 `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js`:
165|  - Fresh `in_stage` work wins over a task with ≥ N consecutive resumes
166|    (survey q2/q3 default: threshold 3, all resume kinds).
167|  - First and second resumes keep Rule-0 priority (fast path pinned).
168|  - Backoff delay: a 3rd-resume task is skipped until 30s elapsed, 4th until
169|    60s, capped at 5min (inject `now` — never wall-clock in the sort).
170|  - Different-runner preference / refusing-runner hide (survey q4): task
171|    hidden from the refusing runner for ~2min while visible to others.
172|- 2.3 Keep-pins (must stay green throughout, no edits): the 5x bare-interrupt
173|  escalation test (`executionLedger.test.js:765-797`), the 5x death-loop
174|  parking test (`taskScheduler.test.js:569-584`), and the reasoned-history
175|  test (`executionLedger.test.js:746-763`, updated only if its
176|  `interruptCount: 1` expectation legitimately becomes 0 — prefer updating
177|  that one assertion with a comment over weakening the test).
178|
179|## 8. Phase 3 — Ledger: exclude cap refusals from death counting
180|
181|File: `api/flow/executionLedger.js` (`interruptExecution`, ~L639-678).
182|
183|- 3.1 Branch on `isCapacityRefusalReason(reason)`:
184|  - Cap refusal: leave `runnerInterruptCount`/`runnerInterruptStage`
185|    untouched; maintain `task.capacityRefusalCount` /
186|    `task.capacityRefusalStage` with the same per-task+stage consecutive
187|    semantics (stage change restarts at 1); still set
188|    `status = "interrupted"`, still record history with the reason, still
189|    `interrupts += 1`; add a `capacityRefusals += 1` monitor counter.
190|  - Return shape: keep `{ interrupted, interruptCount, escalated }` and add
191|    `capacityRefusal: true, capacityRefusalCount` so callers/tests can tell.
192|- 3.2 Operator visibility (survey q1/q5): at `capacityRefusalCount ===
193|  MAX_CAPACITY_REFUSALS_BEFORE_NOTE`, push a history note ("capacity
194|  refusals noted … never parks") — visibility only, no escalation counter,
195|  no parking hook.
196|- 3.3 Reset semantics: `completeExecution` clears the capacity fields exactly
197|  like it clears `runnerInterruptCount`/`runnerInterruptStage`
198|  (`executionLedger.js:540-543`). Document the mixed-streak rule from 2.1.
199|- 3.4 Re-run Phase 0 script: 5 cap interrupts → count 0, no park. Run

202|## 9. Phase 4 — Scheduler: re-dispatch backoff + fresh-work priority
203|
204|Survey defaults: q2 (3 strikes, 30s doubling to 5min, fresh first), q3 (all
205|resumes), q4 (hide from refuser ~2min). New state must be durable on the task
206|(it already persists via `_saveTaskMarkdown`) and time-injectable.
207|
208|- 4.1 Track consecutive resumes per task+stage: add
209|  `task.consecutiveResumes` / `task.consecutiveResumeStage`, incremented in
210|  `autoResumeTask` (`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js`) when the stage
211|  matches (else reset to 1), cleared on completion/stage advancement. New
212|  pure module `api/flow/scheduler/resumeBackoff.js`: `resumeBackoffMs(task,
213|  stageId, nowMs)` → 0 below threshold, else
214|  `min(30s * 2^(n-3), 5min)`. Unit-test the curve incl. cap and garbage
215|  timestamps (follow the `interruptionTimestampMs` collapse-to-0 pattern).
216|- 4.2 Enforce the delay in `findResumedCandidate.js`: skip candidates whose

225|  `scanClaimableTasks.js` (fleet path): without it the runner fleet still
226|  re-claims instantly and the fix only covers the embedded scheduler.
227|- 4.4 Prefer a different runner (survey q4): on a cap refusal, record

229|  `findResumedCandidate` (embedded: skip when the only claimant would be that

240|## 10. Phase 5 — Assurance: tests, gates, and fleet confirmation
241|
242|- 5.1 Red→green: the Phase 2 tests fail on the base tree (record the failure

253|- 5.4 Edge sweep (each gets a test or a written reason it needs none):
254|  null/empty/other reasons, reason with leading whitespace, stage change
255|  mid-streak, completion clearing both counters, corrupt `updatedAt`,
256|  backoff cap at 5min, hide-window expiry, old runners sending no reason
257|  (covered by q3-all-resumes default).
258|
259|## 11. Documentation plan
260|

commit 5b53cbcdd0442209bfd74dee6b8efceaf7e5acc8
Author: Ewrdad Server <[REDACTED EMAIL]>
Date:   Mon Nov 23 13:37:56 2026 +0000

    S1 cleanup stage: harden re-dispatch backoff, co-locate unit tests, verify red/green
    
    - resumeBackoffRemainingMs: clamp remaining delay to the computed backoff so
      a future-dated reference (runner clock skew) can never extend the wait past
      the curve; garbage timestamps still collapse to the epoch (delay 0, never
      a park)
    - fireQueueEmptyPush re-check now uses findNextCandidateTask({ignoreBackoff:true})
      (threaded through findResumedCandidate): a resumed task held in its backoff
      window still counts as pending work, so no false queue-empty page during a
      30s-5min backoff; dispatch paths never pass ignoreBackoff
    - co-located unit tests per KB Code Standards: resumeBackoff.test.js,
      resumeBackoffRemainingMs.test.js, capacityRefusalHide.test.js,
      autoResumeTask.resumeStreak.test.js; fleet-path backoff+hide cases in
      scanClaimableTasks.test.js; queue-empty push case in taskScheduler.push.test.js;
      findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js slimmed to candidate-selection behavior
    - documented that streak counters are in-memory per process (same as the
      pre-existing runnerInterruptCount): a restart restarts the streak at 1,
      which fails safe (backoff can only delay, never park)
    - red/green evidence recorded in docs/tasks/3b82f6ae.../STAGE-CLEANUP-VERIFY.md:
      5 cap refusals park as runner-death-loop on main @6558033, count 0 / no
      escalation / resumable on this branch; 5 bare interrupts still park on both
    - gates: full api suite 474 files / 7688 tests green, lint 0 errors,
      one-function-per-file PASS, jsdoc-example PASS

--- /dev/null
+++ b/api/flow/capacityRefusal.js
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+/***
+ * MARK: CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX
+ * @description Wire prefix a Runner puts on an interrupt when it refuses
+ *   work because its workdir/worktree cap is reached
+ *   (`runner/daemon.js`, WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED): infra exhaustion, not a
+ *   task or runner fault. The ledger matches the TRIMMED reason against
+ *   this prefix to keep capacity refusals out of the runner-death count
+ *   (task 3b82f6ae).
+ * @example CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX => "Runner workdir unavailable:"
+ ***/
+export const CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX = "Runner workdir unavailable:";
+
+/***
+ * MARK: isCapacityRefusalReason
+ * @description Whether an interrupt reason is a capacity refusal (a Runner
+ *   that is simply full) rather than a death/crash. True iff the trimmed
+ *   reason starts with CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX; null, empty,
+ *   non-string, and other reasons (including crash reasons) are false, as
+ *   is a reason that merely contains the prefix later in the string.
+ * @param {*} reason - Raw interrupt reason from the Runner wire.
+ * @returns {boolean}
+ * @example isCapacityRefusalReason("Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5)") => true
+ * @example isCapacityRefusalReason("  Runner workdir unavailable: full ") => true
+ * @example isCapacityRefusalReason("Runner crashed: Runner workdir unavailable: x") => false
+ * @example isCapacityRefusalReason(null) => false
+ ***/
+export function isCapacityRefusalReason(reason) {
+	if (typeof reason !== "string") return false;
+	const trimmed = reason.trim();
+	return trimmed.startsWith(CAPACITY_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX);
+}
diff --git a/api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js b/api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js
index 6aad4516..42857293 100644
--- a/api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js
+++ b/api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js
@@ -36,6 +36,26 @@ export function autoResumeTask(store, projectId, taskId, projectCwd, { reason }
 	task.wasInterrupted = false;
 	task.status = "in_stage";
 	task.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString();
+	// Task 3b82f6ae (S1): count consecutive resumes per task+stage so the
+	// scheduler can slow re-dispatch of a repeatedly interrupted task
+	// (resumeBackoff). A stage change restarts the streak at 1; completion
+	// clears it (executionLedger.completeExecution). Like the
+	// runnerInterruptCount death streak, this counter is in-memory per
+	// process (task markdown does not persist it) — a restart restarts the
+	// streak at 1, which fails safe: the backoff can only ever delay, never
+	// park, and a fresh process always gives the first resumes the fast
+	// path while the live refusal loop rebuilds the streak within seconds.
+	const resumeStageId = task.currentStageId ?? null;
+	if (
+		task.consecutiveResumeStage === resumeStageId &&
+		Number.isInteger(task.consecutiveResumes)
+	) {
+		task.consecutiveResumes += 1;
+	} else {
+		task.consecutiveResumes = 1;
+		task.consecutiveResumeStage = resumeStageId;
+	}
+	task.lastResumedAt = task.updatedAt;
 	if (typeof store._resetAutoIteration === "function") {
 		store._resetAutoIteration(task);
 	}

+/***
+ * MARK: CAPACITY_REFUSAL_HIDE_MS
+ * @description How long a task is hidden from the runner that just
+ *   capacity-refused it (task 3b82f6ae, survey q4): the backend cannot
+ *   direct-assign, so instead the fleet scan omits that one task from that
+ *   one runner's listing for this window (~2min), giving a different runner
+ *   the chance to claim it.
+ * @example CAPACITY_REFUSAL_HIDE_MS => 120000
+ ***/
+export const CAPACITY_REFUSAL_HIDE_MS = 2 * 60_000;
+
+/***
+ * MARK: isCapacityRefusalHidden

+/***
+ * MARK: RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD
+ * @description Consecutive resumes of the same task+stage after which
+ *   re-dispatch slows down (task 3b82f6ae, survey q2): the first resumes
+ *   stay instant (one-off hiccups recover immediately), from this many

+ *   interrupts from older runners are covered too.
+ * @example RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD => 3
+ ***/
+export const RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD = 3;
+
+/***
+ * MARK: RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS
+ * @description First backoff delay once a task+stage reaches
+ *   RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD consecutive resumes (task 3b82f6ae): 30s,
+ *   doubling per further resume.
+ * @example RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS => 30000
+ ***/
+export const RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 30_000;
+
+/***
+ * MARK: RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS
+ * @description Cap on the exponential resume backoff (task 3b82f6ae): 5
+ *   minutes, so a repeatedly interrupted task is never starved forever —
+ *   just slowed enough that a still-full runner cannot re-claim it within
+ *   milliseconds.
+ * @example RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS => 300000
+ ***/
+export const RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 5 * 60_000;
+
+/***
+ * MARK: resumeBackoffMs
+ * @description Total re-dispatch delay for a task+stage given its
+ *   consecutive-resume streak (task 3b82f6ae): 0 below
+ *   RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD (or when the streak belongs to a different
+ *   stage), else `RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS * 2^(n - threshold)` capped at
+ *   RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS — 30s at 3 resumes, 60s at 4, …, 5min cap. Pure:
+ *   no clock reads here; callers inject `now` via
+ *   `resumeBackoffRemainingMs`.
+ * @param {Object} task - Task carrying `consecutiveResumes` / `consecutiveResumeStage`.
+ * @param {string|null} stageId - Stage the candidate would resume into.
+ * @returns {number} Delay in ms (0 = no backoff).
+ * @example resumeBackoffMs({ consecutiveResumes: 2, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1" }, "s1") => 0
+ * @example resumeBackoffMs({ consecutiveResumes: 3, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1" }, "s1") => 30000
+ * @example resumeBackoffMs({ consecutiveResumes: 10, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1" }, "s1") => 300000
+ * @example resumeBackoffMs({ consecutiveResumes: 9, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1" }, "s2") => 0
+ ***/
+export function resumeBackoffMs(task, stageId) {
+	const n = Number.isInteger(task?.consecutiveResumes) ? task.consecutiveResumes : 0;
+	if (n < RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD) return 0;
+	const streakStage = task?.consecutiveResumeStage ?? null;
+	if (streakStage !== stageId) return 0;
+	const steps = n - RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD;
+	return Math.min(RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS * 2 ** steps, RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS);

+import { resumeBackoffMs } from './resumeBackoff.js';
+
+/***
+ * MARK: resumeBackoffRemainingMs
+ * @description How much of a task+stage's resume backoff is still left at
+ *   `nowMs` (task 3b82f6ae): `resumeBackoffMs` minus the time elapsed since
+ *   the task was last offered (`lastResumedAt` from the auto-resume flip,
+ *   else the interruption/entry timestamps), floored at 0. 0 means the
+ *   task may be re-dispatched now. The reference timestamp collapses to 0
+ *   (the epoch) on garbage input — same policy as
+ *   `interruptionTimestampMs` — which makes elapsed huge and the remaining
+ *   delay 0, so a corrupt date can never park a task forever. The result is
+ *   also clamped to the computed backoff, so a future-dated reference
+ *   (clock skew on the writing runner) can never extend the wait past the
+ *   curve. Clock is injected, never read here, so tests pin exact
+ *   boundaries.
+ * @param {Object} task - Task carrying the resume-streak fields.
+ * @param {string|null} stageId - Stage the candidate would resume into.
+ * @param {number} [nowMs=Date.now()] - Clock in ms since epoch (tests inject).
+ * @returns {number} Remaining backoff in ms (0 = dispatchable now).
+ * @example resumeBackoffRemainingMs({ consecutiveResumes: 3, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1", lastResumedAt: "2026-09-24T10:00:00.000Z" }, "s1", Date.parse("2026-09-24T10:00:10.000Z")) => 20000
+ * @example resumeBackoffRemainingMs({ consecutiveResumes: 3, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1", lastResumedAt: "2026-09-24T10:00:00.000Z" }, "s1", Date.parse("2026-09-24T10:01:00.000Z")) => 0
+ ***/
+export function resumeBackoffRemainingMs(task, stageId, nowMs = Date.now()) {
+	const backoff = resumeBackoffMs(task, stageId);
+	if (backoff <= 0) return 0;
+	const now = Number.isFinite(nowMs) ? nowMs : Date.now();
+	const raw =
+		task?.lastResumedAt ||
+		task?.interruptedAt ||
+		task?.updatedAt ||
+		task?.enteredStageAt ||
+		0;
+	const parsed = new Date(raw).getTime();
+	const refMs = Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : 0;
+	// Fail-safe both ways: never negative, and never above the computed
+	// backoff (a future-dated reference from clock skew must not extend
+	// the wait past the curve).
+	return Math.min(backoff, Math.max(0, backoff - (now - refMs)));
+}

+ * MARK: RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS
+ * @description First backoff delay once a task+stage reaches
+ *   RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD consecutive resumes (task 3b82f6ae): 30s,
+ *   doubling per further resume.

+ *   minutes, so a repeatedly interrupted task is never starved forever —
+ *   just slowed enough that a still-full runner cannot re-claim it within
+ *   milliseconds.
+ * @example RESUME_BACKOFF_MAX_MS => 300000
+ ***/

+/***
+ * MARK: resumeBackoffMs

+ *   consecutive-resume streak (task 3b82f6ae): 0 below
+ *   RESUME_BACKOFF_THRESHOLD (or when the streak belongs to a different
+ *   stage), else `RESUME_BACKOFF_BASE_MS * 2^(n - threshold)` capped at

+ * @example resumeBackoffMs({ consecutiveResumes: 2, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1" }, "s1") => 0
+ * @example resumeBackoffMs({ consecutiveResumes: 3, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1" }, "s1") => 30000

+import { resumeBackoffMs } from './resumeBackoff.js';

+/***
+ * MARK: resumeBackoffRemainingMs
+ * @description How much of a task+stage's resume backoff is still left at
+ *   `nowMs` (task 3b82f6ae): `resumeBackoffMs` minus the time elapsed since
+ *   the task was last offered (`lastResumedAt` from the auto-resume flip,
+ *   else the interruption/entry timestamps), floored at 0. 0 means the
+ *   task may be re-dispatched now. The reference timestamp collapses to 0
+ *   (the epoch) on garbage input — same policy as
+ *   `interruptionTimestampMs` — which makes elapsed huge and the remaining
+ *   delay 0, so a corrupt date can never park a task forever. The result is
+ *   also clamped to the computed backoff, so a future-dated reference
+ *   (clock skew on the writing runner) can never extend the wait past the
+ *   curve. Clock is injected, never read here, so tests pin exact
+ *   boundaries.
+ * @param {Object} task - Task carrying the resume-streak fields.
+ * @param {string|null} stageId - Stage the candidate would resume into.
+ * @param {number} [nowMs=Date.now()] - Clock in ms since epoch (tests inject).
+ * @returns {number} Remaining backoff in ms (0 = dispatchable now).
+ * @example resumeBackoffRemainingMs({ consecutiveResumes: 3, consecutiveResumeStage: "s1", lastResumedAt: "2026-09-24T10:00:00.000Z" }, "s1", Date.parse("2026-09-24T10:00:10.000Z")) => 20000

+ ***/

+	const backoff = resumeBackoffMs(task, stageId);
+	if (backoff <= 0) return 0;
+	const now = Number.isFinite(nowMs) ? nowMs : Date.now();
+	const raw =

+		task?.interruptedAt ||
+		task?.updatedAt ||
+		task?.enteredStageAt ||
+		0;
+	const parsed = new Date(raw).getTime();
+	const refMs = Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : 0;

+	// backoff (a future-dated reference from clock skew must not extend
+	// the wait past the curve).
+	return Math.min(backoff, Math.max(0, backoff - (now - refMs)));

+# Stage verification — S1 cleanup/rigidify pass (task 3b82f6ae)
+
+This note records the red/green evidence and the cleanup-stage hardening for
+the backend change: capacity refusals excluded from the runner-death count +
+re-dispatch backoff (30s doubling to 5min after 3 consecutive resumes) +
+refusing-runner hide window (~2min) on the fleet scan.
+
+## Red/green repro (GUIDE-01 §3 equivalent, run locally)
+
+Script: 5 interrupts with `reason: "Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap
+reached (~5)"` on the same task+stage via `ExecutionLedger.interruptExecution`,
+then `isAutoResumableWithReason(task, { type: "agent" })`.
+
+| Tree | runnerInterruptCount | escalated | interruptEscalations | capacityRefusalCount | parked as runner-death-loop |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| base `main` @ 6558033 (worktree) | 5 | true | 1 | n/a (field absent) | **true (bug reproduced)** |
+| branch `kb/3b82f6ae` (fix) | 0 | false | 0 | 5 | **false — resumable** |
+
+Pin (must hold on both trees): 5 BARE interrupts (no reason) →
+`interruptCount 5, escalated true, parkedAsDeathLoop true` on base AND branch.
+Confirmed identical — true death streaks still park.
+
+## Cleanup-stage changes (this stage)
+
+- `resumeBackoffRemainingMs`: result now also clamped to the computed
+  backoff, so a future-dated reference timestamp (runner clock skew) can
+  never extend the wait past the curve. Fail-safe both directions.
+- `fireQueueEmptyPush` re-check now calls `findNextCandidateTask(store,
+  { ignoreBackoff: true })` (threaded through to `findResumedCandidate`):
+  a resumed task held in its backoff window still counts as pending work,
+  so the queue must not page the operator as "empty" while it waits out a
+  30s–5min delay. Dispatch paths never pass `ignoreBackoff`.
+- Co-located unit tests added next to each new module per KB Code
+  Standards: `scheduler/resumeBackoff.test.js`,
+  `scheduler/resumeBackoffRemainingMs.test.js`,
+  `scheduler/capacityRefusalHide.test.js`,
+  `scheduler/autoResumeTask.resumeStreak.test.js` (streak increment / stage
+  reset / corrupt-streak fail-safe / null stage / idempotency),
+  plus fleet-path backoff+hide cases in `dispatch/scanClaimableTasks.test.js`
+  and an `ignoreBackoff` case + a queue-empty-push case
+  (`taskScheduler.push.test.js`).
+  `findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js` was slimmed to candidate-selection
+  behavior only (pure-function curves moved to their co-located files).
+- Documented that the resume/death streak counters are in-memory per
+  process (same as the pre-existing `runnerInterruptCount`; task markdown
+  does not persist them): after a restart the streak restarts at 1, which
+  fails safe — backoff can only delay, never park.
+
+## Durability / continuity of operations
+
+- Ledger: cap refusals still set `status: "interrupted"` and record the
+  reason in history (with_reason stays visible); only the death counter is
+  excluded. Completion clears all streak fields. Stage change restarts
+  both counters per task+stage.
+- Scheduler polls on an interval, so a backed-off task re-enters candidacy
+  automatically when the delay elapses — no timer or manual kick needed;
+  no path can strand the task (backoff is time-based, capped at 5min).
+- Fleet path: `scanClaimableTasks` honors the same backoff and hides the
+  task from the refusing runner (`runnerId` plumbed from
+  `runnerRoutes.js` dispatch scan) for ~2min; all other runners still see
+  it. The hide fails open (expired/garbage/missing → visible).
+- Garbage handling everywhere: corrupt timestamps collapse to the epoch
+  (delay 0 / hide expired — never a park); non-integer streaks read as 0;
+  null task/reason safe.
+
+## Gates (this stage)
+
+- `npx vitest run` on all touched files: 50+ tests green (see run output).
+- Full `npm run test:api`, `npm run lint:api`,
+  `node scripts/check-one-function-per-file.mjs`,
+  `node scripts/check-jsdoc-example.mjs` — see stage output; all green.

{"path":"docs/tasks/3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7/UPGRADE-SAFETY-REVIEW.md","content":"# Upgrade-safety review — S1 (task 3b82f6ae)

Stage question: will the current implementation break existing installs on
update? Scope reviewed: `main...origin/kb/3b82f6ae-8c54-44bf-b283-0ffab76e7ab7`
@ `5b53cbcd` (13 source files, 9 test files, 2 docs). Read-only review
(`git show` / grep / `node --check` / runtime probes); no source edited.
Verdict: NO upgrade break found — update is backward-compatible.

## Persistence: no migration, no disk-format change

- `saveTaskMarkdown` (`api/work/taskPersistence.js:68-114`) writes frontmatter
  from an explicit allowlist. None of the new fields (`runnerInterruptCount`,
  `capacityRefusalCount`, `consecutiveResumes`, `lastCapacityRefusal`,
  `lastResumedAt`) are in it, so they are in-memory only and `task.md` bytes
  are identical before/after (history lines only).
- `parseTaskMarkdown` (`taskPersistence.js:994+`) reconstructs tasks from a
  fixed key list; new fields start `undefined` after restart/load. Every new
  reader is null-safe (`Number.isInteger(...) ? : 0`, `?? null`, `task?.`),
  so old files and missing fields cannot throw.
- Restart resets streaks to the fast path (same as pre-existing
  `runnerInterruptCount`); backoff can only delay, never park. Already-parked
  tasks are not stuck worse than before (park state was in-memory anyway).

## Signatures and API shape: additive-only, optional params

- `findResumedCandidate(store, {now, ignoreBackoff}={})`,
  `findNextCandidateTask(..., {now, ignoreBackoff})`,
  `scanClaimableTasks(deps, {runnerId, now})` — all new params optional with
  defaults; every old caller (`scheduleTick`, `taskStore`, `runnerRoutes`)
  keeps working. Verified call sites: `scheduleTick.js:157`,
  `taskStore.js:921,1061`, `runnerRoutes.js:1375` (new call passes `runnerId`).
- `interruptExecution` return: non-capacity path returns the identical
  `{interrupted, interruptCount, escalated}`; the capacity path adds fields
  only. The sole caller (`runnerRoutes.js:1077`) returns it as JSON; old
  runners ignore extras. No runner rollout needed (prefix already sent by
  existing runners via `daemon.js:2306`).
- No config, env, dependency, or `package.json` changes; no frontend changes.
- `isAutoResumableWithReason.js` change is comment-only; death-loop branch
  unchanged and still keys only off `runnerInterruptCount`.

## Runtime probes (executed, read-only, Node v24.22.2)

- `node --check --input-type=module` on all 10 touched/new modules: PASS.
- Classifier (`capacityRefusal.js`): `[null,"",42] -> false,false,false`;
  plain/leading-space prefix -> `true,true`.
- Backoff: `[null,{}, "x", 1.5, n=3, wrong-stage, n=10] -> [0,0,0,0,30000,0,300000]`.
- Remaining: `[null, garbage-ref, 30s-10s, future-ref, wrong-stage] ->
  [0,0,20000,300000,0]` (future clock-skew ref clamps to the curve).
- Hide: garbage/missing task -> false (fail-open). Garbage `at` returns true
  only for the unrealistic `now=1000`; with a real clock (~1.7e12) it is
  false — not a production break.

## Dispatch/recovery behavior on update

- First resumes stay instant (backoff threshold 3; fresh installs have no
  streaks). Backoff is capped at 5min, time-based, re-checked every poll —
  no stranding, no manual step.
- Startup recovery (`startupRecovery.js:101`) and `scheduleTick` use
  `autoResumeTask`/`findNextCandidateTask` directly; recovery is not blocked
  by backoff. Queue display (`getScheduledQueue.js`) uses its own checks,
  not `findResumedCandidate`, so backed-off work stays visible.
- `fireQueueEmptyPush` re-check now passes `ignoreBackoff:true`, so a
  backed-off task still counts as pending (no false queue-empty page).

## Caveat

Full `npm run test:api` was not re-run against the origin tree in this
docs-only stage (would require checking out non-docs code); relying on the
recorded gates in `STAGE-CLEANUP-VERIFY.md` plus the static compat analysis
and probes above. The decisive question — old installs updating without
crash, migration, or stuck tasks — is answered by that analysis.
"}
